name: nested-sections-error-format-reconciled
body:
source: plan review of nested-sections escalated a spec-level inconsistency between requirements.requirement.nested-section-validation and the existing global requirement requirements.requirement.error-reporting. The feature request's illustrative error example `slides/3-columns.md:42 columns[2].blocks[1]: unknown field "lable" (did you mean "label"?)` used a dot-and-parenthesis notation that differs from the canonical, implemented and tested kalide format: ` › ` (U+203A) path joins, indexed segments rendered `name[i]`, and the fix appended after ` — ` (verified in internal/validate/validate.go segmentSeparator/Format, internal/template/checkvalues.go PathString and ValueError.Error, and the deck error page / generated AGENTS.md).

Decision [with user — coordinator, user away]: KEEP the existing ` › ` format as canonical. The source's dot/parenthesis example is an informal paraphrase; the source lists no decision to change the global error format, and adopting it would be a large unrequested change to implemented, tested behaviour. Nested containment errors simply extend the existing notation to arbitrary depth — path segments joined with ` › `, an indexed segment rendered `name[i]`, and the fix appended after ` — `.

Resolution: rewrote requirements.requirement.nested-section-validation's illustrative error and its AC to the canonical form (`slides/3-columns.md:42 › columns[2] › blocks[1]: unknown field "lable" — did you mean "label"?`, parent path `columns[2] › blocks`) and stated explicitly that the nested containment path reuses the error-reporting format at any depth. Added to requirements.requirement.error-reporting a sentence that the path form extends to nested section instances (e.g. `columns[2] › blocks[1]`); its canonical example is unchanged. This note records the deliberate deviation from the source's illustrative example so the human gate can see it.
